question: to the Commission Elena Kountoura (The Left) Subject:

European legislation1 provides for exemptions from duties, excise duty and VAT for Member States on goods intended for the supply of international ships, without distinction as to the invoiced party. In Greece, under national regulations2, exemptions are granted only when the goods are invoiced directly to the ship owner or operator, excluding catering companies and concessionaires operating on ships. Exemptions also do not apply to entire categories of vessels, such as professional pleasure boats on international voyages, international ferry liners and seagoing vessels. No such restrictions appear to be in place in the other Member States. This means that Greek products and businesses providing ship supply services lose a significant share of the relevant market and that ship supply services in Greek ports are outsourced to businesses in other Member States3, leading to a distortion of competition to the detriment of Greek businesses. Since the memoranda of the sectors concerned have not remedied the problem, can the Commission say: 1.
Does it consider that the above restrictions in Greece are compatible with EU law, the principle of equal treatment and the level playing field in the internal market?
What is its assessment of the link between exemptions and invoiced parties, when this is not explicitly provided for in EU law?
What steps does it intend to take to ensure the proper and uniform application of the exemptions in all Member States?

See Article 132 of Regulation (EC) No 1186/2009, which gives Member States the option of adopting provisions on exemptions, as well as Directive 2006/112/EC on VAT and Directive (EU) 2020/262 on excise duty, which provide for the possibility of exempting all products from the relevant taxes. 2 See Article 36(3) of Law 5222/2025 and Article 32(1) of Law 5144/24 on the exemption from duties, excise duty, tax on consumption and VAT respectively, of goods intended for the supply of ships, including food supplies, drinks, fuel and lubricants, etc. 3 Sectoral stakeholders already sent a memorandum to the Independent Authority for Public Revenue (AADE) in 2025 (see https://libertypress.gr/efodiasmos-ploivn-aade/). 1
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (25.8.2026) Article 148(a) of Council Directive 2006/112/EC (the VAT (value-added tax) Directive)1 provides that supplies of goods for the fuelling and provisioning of vessels used on the high seas are to be exempt from VAT. The exemption applies only to vessels used for navigation on the high seas and carrying passengers for reward or used for commercial, industrial or fishing activities, as well as to vessels used for rescue or assistance at sea or for inshore fishing, with the exception, in the case of the latter, of ships’ provisions. The Court held that the exemption applies only to the supply of goods to a vessel operator who will use those goods for fuelling and provisioning and cannot be extended to the supply of those goods effected at a previous stage in the commercial chain2. Therefore the fact that the exemption is granted only when the goods are invoiced directly to the ship owner or operator does not seem to be in breach of EU Law. As regards excise duties, Article 13 of Council Directive (EU) 2020/262 allows Member States to exempt excise goods supplied on board a ship during the sea-crossing to a third territory or a third country. Member States must take the measures necessary to prevent any possible evasion, avoidance or abuse. The production, processing, holding and storage of excise goods is covered by Chapter III of this Directive, whereas the movement of excise goods under suspension of excise duty is governed in Chapter IV thereof. Regarding customs duties, according to the Union Customs Code, no such duties apply to ship supplies, except for cases of non-compliance with the obligations regarding the customs supervision, movement, or exit of the goods out of the customs territory of the EU.
1 Council Directive 2006/112/EC of 28 November 2006 on the common system of value added tax (OJ L 347,

11.12.2006, p. 1). 2 Judgment of 26 June 1990, Velker International Oil Company Ltd NV, C-185/89, EU:C:1990:262; paragraph 22; Judgment of 14 September 2006, Elmeka NE, Joined cases C-181/04 to C-183/04, EU:C:2006:563, paragraph 25; Judgment of 3 September 2015, UAB "Fast Bunkering Klaipėda“, C-526/13, EU:C:2015:536, paragraph 29.
